note: Typed tool routes this game project uses. Declared when the game is created and amendable at any time with `forge.py mcp add|remove|enable|disable`. This file is the project's truth: the host-specific MCP surface is rendered from it, so a session started from this project sees the servers regardless of what the machine had configured when the project was made.
rules: An entry naming a provider in dependencies/route-registry.json inherits its capabilities, lane, isolation mode and fallbacks. Do not restate them here.
An entry naming anything else must declare server, capabilities, lane, isolation_mode and fallbacks itself, so routing can still resolve it.
Rendering preserves servers this file does not declare. Forge only owns the entries listed here.
A transport declares either a command the host starts or a url it calls. Unreal's first-party server is hosted by the editor, so it is a url and Forge never starts it.

servers.note: Unreal Engine's first-party Unreal MCP plugin, Experimental since 5.8. Enable ModelContextProtocol and AllToolsets in the .uproject and keep the editor open. Enabling them is necessary and not sufficient: the server only listens when asked, so launch with -ModelContextProtocolStartServer, set bAutoStartServer, or run ModelContextProtocol.StartServer in the editor console. `forge.py route-status` handshakes this endpoint and reports AVAILABLE_VERIFIED only when it answers; until then the route degrades to its declared fallback. Change the url here if the editor serves on another port.
